record: LZ 2026-09 high-recoil candidate event - 2026-11-01 KIV re-evaluation decision

primary_paper.title: ALP-mediated inelastic dark matter and the LUX-ZEPLIN high-recoil candidate event LZ230616
primary_paper.nature: Third-party single-event INTERPRETATION (two-state Majorana DM, gluonic ALP portal, endothermic 1N->2N via operator O6, WimPyDD nuclear responses, SHM v0=238 km/s, vesc=544 km/s, rho=0.3 GeV/cm^3, exposure 2.84 tonne-years)
primary_paper.statistic_self_description: "neither reproduces the official LZ likelihood nor defines statistically calibrated confidence regions"

sigma_dm_nucleon_limit_status.what_the_paper_reports_instead: Required coupling product |g_G| to produce ONE expected event in 5.4-269.9 keV under a conditional single-event signal hypothesis (a signal-interpretation statement, not an exclusion limit)
sigma_dm_nucleon_limit_status.why_not_comparable_to_channel_5: Channel 5's observable is elastic spin-independent sigma_DM-nucleon via dark-photon kinetic mixing. 2609.08893v1 constrains an ALP-gluon coupling product for an inelastic two-state model with momentum-dependent O6 nucleon operator; it converts nothing to a sigma_SI limit.

companion_papers.note: Aristizabal Sierra+ - neutrino up-scattering limits (sterile fermion couplings, NOT sigma_DM-nucleon); concludes up-scattering does not explain the event
Gu+ - inelastic-xenon excitation companion channel, rate O(0.1) of elastic or below
Jeesun & Majumdar+ - atmospheric-neutrino up-scattering interpretation (pseudoscalar mediator, y_chi/y_u region)

lz_paper_significance.source: PDF text re-read 2026-11-01 from docs/papers/verified/2609.02823_lz_2026.pdf: "global significance of 2.6 when accounting for look-elsewhere effects, with a maximum local significance of 3.4 across the models tested"
lz_paper_significance.lz_new_limits_in_same_paper: Two-sided 90% CL intervals on NREFT operator couplings (Fig 6; O1s inelastic at 1000 GeV, Ls10 elastic) described as world-leading FOR THOSE MODELS, plus an O1s recast to inelastic DM-nucleon cross-section with scalar normalization (Fig S7). None of these replaces the elastic SI WS2024 curve used by Channel 5.

channel5_comparison.t30_source: LZ_REAL table in v0.3-prelim/code/t30_lz_real_posterior.py (HEPData 155182, arXiv:2410.17036, 26 mass points 9 GeV - 10 TeV, log-log interpolation in loglike_lz_real)
channel5_comparison.mapping: sigma_SI_from_dark_photon (t39_tier3_epsilon_alpha_joint_fit.py) with alpha_D taken as the posterior alpha_X
channel5_comparison.note: The older MODEL_ASSUMPTIONS figure "1.5e-46 at 770 GeV" came from the superseded placeholder table in channels_extended.py; the real-curve value is 2.337e-47 cm^2.
